finding.claim: deleteAccount never enforces authorization: the canDelete result is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any account by id (IDOR / broken object-level authorization).
finding.source: Path parameter `id` and caller identity `u` in deleteAccount(User u, long id), reachable via DELETE /accounts/{id} by any authenticated non-admin user.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-chosen id
accounts.get(id) loads any account with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) evaluated but boolean result discarded

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) implements admin-or-owner but is not enforced on this path; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) throws on denial but is not called here; no other check in this file. Caller authentication lives outside this file and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) is called at line 22 but its boolean result is discarded as a bare statement; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) exists but is not called in deleteAccount; no other check exists in the codebase (grep finds no route/filter for DELETE /accounts). The only guard that would block the call is the caller authentication, which is outside this code and does not check ownership.
verdict.reason: Line 22 `canDelete(u, a);` discards its boolean result and line 23 `accounts.remove(id)` runs unconditionally (src/AccountService.java:22-23), so any authenticated user who is neither admin nor owner of account `id` can delete it, while the correct check exists at line 29 in closeAccount but is missing here.

finding.claim: Null dereference for missing accounts lets a non-admin distinguish nonexistent ids (500 NPE) from existing non-owned ids (403 SecurityException), enabling account id enumeration.
finding.source: Path parameter `id` from a non-admin caller of closeAccount (and deleteAccount) at src/AccountService.java:27-29 and 20-22.
finding.sink: Null dereference a.ownerId() in canDelete at src/AccountService.java:10, reached via assertCanDelete at line 29 and canDelete at line 22.

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null for nonexistent id
u.admin() false for non-admin, so a.ownerId() dereferences null -> NullPointerException (500)
For existing non-owned account, canDelete returns false and SecurityException is thrown (403-type response)

finding.guards_checked: u.admin() short-circuit at line 10 prevents the NPE only for admins; no null check after accounts.get in either method. Severity is low because finding F1 already lets any authenticated user delete any account.

verdict.guard_found: none. There is no null check after accounts.get at src/AccountService.java:28 or line 21. The only guard, the u.admin() short-circuit at line 10, applies to admins and does not help non-admins. The SecurityException at line 15 is only reached for existing accounts, so the response difference is real.
verdict.reason: For a non-admin caller, closeAccount with a missing id reaches the null dereference at src/AccountService.java:10 via line 29, while an existing non-owned id throws SecurityException at line 15, so the two responses differ and act as an existence oracle. The 500 and 403 status mapping is not in the repo, so that part is assumed, and the severity is marginal given F1.
